B. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on Burden on Competition
The Exchange does not believe that the proposed rule change will impose any burden on competition that is not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Act. The Exchange does not believe that the proposed rule change will impose any burden on intramarket competition that is not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Act, because the proposed rule change to use the Closing Price to determine the settlement price of ByRDs option contracts will apply equally to all market participants who wish to trade such options on the same terms and in the same manner (including with respect to the payout terms and amount). All market participants will be subject to the same rules applicable to ByRDs option contracts, as described in this proposed rule change. Except as set forth in this proposed rule change, ByRDs option contracts will trade in the same manner as other options on the Exchange.
The Exchange does not believe the proposed rule change will impose any burden on intermarket competition that is not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Act, because other options exchanges may propose similar binary options. Additionally, substantively similar products to ByRDs option contracts are available in the OTC market and various other trading platforms.
The Exchange notes that it operates in a highly competitive market in which market participants can readily direct order flow to competing venues who offer similar products. The Exchange believes the proposed rule change will provide investors with a comparable alternative to the OTC market and other trading venues. The Exchange believes it may be a more attractive alternative to the OTC market and these other venues, as market participants will benefit from being able to trade these options in an exchange environment, which provides, among other things: (1) enhanced efficiency in initiating and closing out positions; (2) increased market transparency; and (3) heightened contra-party creditworthiness. As a result, the Exchange believes that the proposed rule change may relieve any burden on, or otherwise promote, competition, as it will allow the Exchange to offer a securities exchange-listed alternative to the products currently available in these other markets.

and subparagraph (f)(6) of Rule 19b-4 thereunder.
[
32
]
A proposed rule change filed under Rule 19b-4(f)(6)
[
33
]
normally does not become operative prior to 30 days after the date of the filing. However, pursuant to Rule 19b-4(f)(6)(iii),
[
34
]
the Commission may designate a shorter time if such action is consistent with the protection of investors and the public interest. The Exchange has asked the Commission to waive the 30-day operative delay so that the proposed rule change may become operative upon filing. The proposed rule change is designed to provide market participants with additional trading and hedging opportunities that could be better tailored to their investment objectives. The Exchange has proposed heightened eligibility criteria that would limit the underlying equity securities on which the Exchange could list a ByRDs option contract to 100 highly-liquid securities. This limitation should help mitigate the impact (if any) of ByRDs on the closing process of the underlying equity securities and the concern that using an equity security's Closing Price to determine the settlement price at expiration for a ByRDs option contract overlying that equity security could cause excessive volatility or an increased potential for manipulation at the close in the underlying security. For these reasons, the Commission finds that waiver of the 30-day operative delay is consistent with the protection of investors and the public interest. Accordingly, the Commission hereby waives the operative delay and designates the proposal operative upon filing.
[
35
]
At any time within 60 days of the filing of the proposed rule change, the Commission summarily may temporarily suspend such rule change if it appears to the Commission that such action is necessary or appropriate in the public interest, for the protection of investors, or otherwise in furtherance of the purposes of the Act. If the Commission takes such action, the Commission will institute proceedings to determine whether the proposed rule change should be approved or disapproved.
IV. Solicitation of Comments
Interested persons are invited to submit written data, views and arguments concerning the foregoing, including whether the proposed rule change is consistent with the Act. Comments may be submitted by any of the following methods:
Electronic Comments
Use the Commission's internet comment form (
https://www.sec.gov/​rules/​sro.shtml
); or
Send an email to
rule-comments@sec.gov
.
Please include file number SR-NYSEAMER-2026-96 on the subject line.
Paper Comments
Send paper comments in triplicate to Secretary, Securities and Exchange Commission, 100 F Street NE, Washington, DC 20549-1090.
All submissions should refer to file number SR-NYSEAMER-2026-96. This file number should be included on the subject line if email is used. To help the Commission process and review your comments more efficiently, please use only one method. The Commission will post all comments on the Commission's internet website (
https://www.sec.gov/​rules/​sro.shtml
). Copies of the filing will be available for inspection and copying at the principal office of the Exchange. Do not include personal identifiable information in submissions; you should submit only information that you wish
(
printed page 68571)
to make available publicly. We may redact in part or withhold entirely from publication submitted material that is obscene or subject to copyright protection. All submissions should refer to file number SR-NYSEAMER-2026-96 and should be submitted on or before November 30, 2026.
For the Commission, by the Division of Trading and Markets, pursuant to delegated authority.

]

full_text:

Securities and Exchange Commission
[Release No. 34-106742; File No. SR-NYSEAMER-2026-92]
October 27, 2026.
Pursuant to Section 19(b)(1)
[
1
]
of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (“Act”)
[
2
]
and Rule 19b-4 thereunder,
[
3
]
notice is hereby given that, on October 14, 2026, NYSE American LLC (“NYSE American” or the “Exchange”) filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission (the “Commission”) the proposed rule change as described in Items I and II below, which Items have been prepared by the self-regulatory organization. The Commission is publishing this notice to solicit comments on the proposed rule change from interested persons.
I. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Terms of Substance of the Proposed Rule Change
The Exchange proposes to (a) amend Article I, Sections 1.05 and 1.06 of its operating agreement to reflect the change of the address of the registered office; (b) amend Article II, Section 2.02 of its operating agreement to change cross references; (c) amend Article II, Section 2.03(a) of its operating agreement to reflect the inclusion of Limited Underwriting Members as members, and (d) make certain clarifying, technical and conforming changes to the operating agreement. The proposed rule change is available on the Exchange's website at
www.nyse.com
and at the principal office of the Exchange.
II. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Purpose of, and Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
In its filing with the Commission, the self-regulatory organization included statements concerning the purpose of, and basis for, the proposed rule change and discussed any comments it received on the proposed rule change. The text of those statements may be examined at the places specified in Item IV below. The Exchange has prepared summaries, set forth in sections A, B, and C below, of the most significant parts of such statements.
A. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Purpose of, and the Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
1. Purpose
The Exchange proposes to amend Article I, Sections 1.05 (Registered Office) and 1.06 (Registered Agent) of the Thirteenth Amended and Restated Operating Agreement of the Exchange (“Operating Agreement”) to reflect the change of the address of the registered office; (b) amend Article II, Section 2.02 (Rules; Supervision of Member Organizations) of the Operating agreement to change cross references; (c) amend Article II, Section 2.03(a) (Board) of the Operating Agreement to reflect the inclusion of Limited Underwriting Members as members, and (c) make certain clarifying, technical and conforming changes to the operating agreement.
Proposed Amendments to Article I, Sections 1.05 and 1.06
The Exchange proposes to amend the Operating Agreement to make a technical change updating the address of the registered office of the registered agent in the state of Delaware. The changes are non-substantive technical administrative changes.
The Exchange is a limited liability company organized under the laws of the state of Delaware. As such, it has and maintains a registered office and registered agent in Delaware.
[
4
]
Article I, Section 1.05 of the Operating Agreement provides that the address of the registered office of the Exchange in the State of Delaware is
(
printed page 68561)
c/o United Agent Group Inc., 3411 Silverside Road, Tatnall Building No. 104, Wilmington, County of New Castle, State of Delaware, 19810. The Exchange proposes to amend such provision to provide that the address is c/o United Agent Group Inc., 1521 Concord Pike, Suite 201, Wilmington, County of New Castle, State of Delaware 19813.
Article I, Section 1.06 of the Operating Agreement provides that the address of the registered agent of the Exchange for service of process on the Exchange in the State of Delaware is Silverside Road, Tatnall Building No. 104, Wilmington, County of New Castle, State of Delaware 19810. The Exchange proposes to amend such provision to provide that the address is 1521 Concord Pike, Suite 201, Wilmington, County of New Castle, State of Delaware 19813.
Proposed Amendments to Article II, Section 2.02
The Exchange proposes to amend Section 2.02 to change the cross references. Currently, Section 2.02 refers to members and member organizations “as defined in Rule 18 and 24 of the Company, respectively” and to specialists and designated market makers “as defined in Rule 2 of the Company Rules”. Because the cross references are no longer correct, the Exchange proposes to make a more general reference to the Exchange's rules. The changes are non-substantive.
To that end, the Exchange proposes to make the following changes to the first two sentences of Section 2.02 (proposed additions italicized, proposed deletions in brackets):
In furtherance and not in limitation of the foregoing, the Board shall have general supervision over members and member organizations [(as defined in Rules 18 and 24 of the Company, respectively)] of the Company (collectively, “Member Organizations”) and over approved persons [(as defined in Rule 25 of the Company)]
as these terms are defined in the Company's Rules
in connection with their conduct with or affecting Member Organizations. The Board may examine into the business conduct and financial condition of Member Organizations, shall have supervision over partnership and corporate arrangements and over all offices of Member Organizations, whether foreign or domestic, and over all persons employed by such Member Organizations (and may, by affirmative vote of a majority of the Directors then in office, adopt, amend or repeal rules with respect to the employment, compensation and duties of such employees), shall have supervision relating to the collection, dissemination and use of quotations and of reports of prices on the exchange operated by the Company, shall have the power to approve or disapprove of any connection or means of communication with the floor and may require the discontinuance of any such connection or means of communication, may disapprove of any member acting as a specialist, designated market maker [(as defined in Rule 2 of the Company Rules)] (“DMM”) or odd lot dealer
as these terms are defined in the Company's Rules,
and may, by affirmative vote of a majority of the Directors then in office, adopt, amend or repeal any rules as it may deem necessary or appropriate in connection with any of the foregoing, including, without limitation, rules relating to: the discipline of Member Organizations, approved persons and registered and non-registered employees of Member Organizations for the violation of applicable law or the rules of the Company; and the arbitration of any controversy between parties who are Member Organizations and any controversy between a Member Organization and any other person arising out of the business of such Member Organization.
Proposed Amendments to Article II, Section 2.03(a)
The Exchange Act requires that every exchange have rules that “assure a fair representation of its members in the selection of its directors and administration of its affairs”.
[
5
]
In compliance with this requirement, the Exchange sets forth, in Article II, Section 2.03(a) of its Operating Agreement, the process by which its fair representation directors, the “Non-Affiliated Directors,” are chosen. The Exchange now proposes to amend Article II, Section 2.03(a) of the Operating Agreement to ensure that it remains in compliance with the cited Exchange Act requirement.
More specifically, the Exchange proposes to amend the Operating Agreement consistent with a recent filing by the Exchange to add a new membership category known as “Limited Underwriting Members.” Limited Underwriting Members are a type of non-trading Exchange membership solely for the limited purpose of acting as a principal underwriter of an underwritten public offering.
[
6
]
As such, they do not have trading permits. Accordingly, the Exchange proposes to amend Section 2.03(a)(iv) and (v) to state that member organizations that do not have trading permits may both sign petitions and vote in any election for fair representation directors. The proposed change is designed to ensure that all “members” (as defined in the Exchange Act) have “fair representation . . . in the selection of its directors and administration of its affairs”.
[
7
]
To that end, the Exchange proposes to make the following changes to Section 2.03(a) (proposed additions italicized):
(iv) Petition Candidates. * * * * * For purposes of determining whether a person has been endorsed by the requisite ten percent (10%) of signatures to be a Petition Candidate, each Member Organization in good standing shall be entitled to one signature for each 86 Trinity Permit (as the term is defined in the rules of the Company), equity trading permit or options trading permit issued by the Company owned by it
, and each Member Organization in good standing that does not own a trading permit shall be entitled to one signature;
provided, however, that no Member Organization, either alone or together with its affiliates as defined under Rule 12b-2 under the Exchange Act (“Affiliates”), may account for more than fifty percent (50%) of the signatures endorsing a particular Petition Candidate, and any signatures of such Member Organization, either alone or together with its Affiliates, in excess of such fifty percent (50%) limitation shall be disregarded.
*
*
*
*
*
(v) Voting. * * * * * For purposes of determining which candidates received the highest number of votes and therefore should be the Fair Representation Candidates nominated by the NYSE American DCRC, each Member Organization in good standing shall be entitled to one vote for each 86 Trinity Permit (as the term is defined in the rules of the Company), equity trading permit or options trading permit issued by the Company owned by it
, and each Member Organization in good standing that does not own a trading permit shall be entitled to one vote;
provided, however, that no Member Organization, either alone or together with its Affiliates, may account for more than twenty percent (20%) of the votes cast for a candidate, and any votes cast by such Member Organization, either alone or together with its Affiliates, in excess of such twenty percent (20%) limitation shall be disregarded.
The proposed change would make the Operating Agreement consistent with the operating agreement of the Exchange's affiliate New York Stock Exchange LLC. More specifically, Article II, Section 2.03(a)(iv) of the Fourteenth Amended and Restated
(
printed page 68562)
Operating Agreement of the New York Stock Exchange provides that “each Member Organization in good standing that does not own a Trading License shall be entitled to one signature” and Section 2.03(a)(v) of the same operating agreement provides that “each Member Organization in good standing that does not own a Trading License shall be entitled to one vote”.
[
8
]
Additional Proposed Amendments
The Exchange proposes to make the following non-substantive technical and conforming changes to the title, recitals and signature page of the Operating Agreement:
Update references to the “Thirteenth Amended and Restated Operating Agreement” to the “Fourteenth Amended and Restated Operating Agreement.”
Update the dates in the introduction and signature line.
Update the recitals.
2. Statutory Basis
The Exchange believes that the proposed rule change is consistent with Section 6(b) of the Exchange Act,
[
9
]
in general, and furthers the objectives of Section 6(b)(1)
[
10
]
in particular, in that it enables the Exchange to be so organized as to have the capacity to be able to carry out the purposes of the Exchange Act and to comply, and to enforce compliance by its exchange members and persons associated with its exchange members, with the provisions of the Exchange Act, the rules and regulations thereunder, and the rules of the Exchange. The Exchange also believes that the proposed rule change is consistent with Section 6(b)(3) of the Exchange Act,
[
11
]
in that it would ensure a fair representation of its members in the selection of its directors and administration of its affairs. The Exchange also believes that the proposed rule change is consistent with Section 6(b)(5) of the Exchange Act,
[
12
]
in that it is designed to prevent fraudulent and manipulative acts and practices, to promote just and equitable principles of trade, to foster cooperation and coordination with persons engaged in facilitating transactions in securities, to remove impediments to and perfect the mechanism of a free and open market and a national market system and, in general, to protect investors and the public interest.
The proposed rule changes to Article I, Article II, Section 2.02, and the additional proposed amendments (together, the “Non-Substantive Changes”) are non-substantive changes that do not impact the governance or ownership of the Exchange. The Exchange believes that the proposed Non-Substantive Changes would enable the Exchange to continue to be so organized as to have the capacity to carry out the purposes of the Exchange Act and comply and enforce compliance with the provisions of the Exchange Act by its members and persons associated with its members, because identifying the registered office in Delaware, making cross-references more accurate, and making conforming changes to the title and date of the Operating Agreement would contribute to the orderly operation of the Exchange by adding clarity and transparency to its rules.
The proposed rule change to Sections 2.03(a)(iv) and (v) would be consistent with the recent filing setting forth, among other things, that Limited Underwriting Members are members, consistent with the definition of “member” in the Exchange Act, by stating that member organizations that do not have trading permits may both sign petitions and vote in any election for fair representation directors.
The proposed rule change to Sections 2.03(a)(iv) and (v) would allow the Exchange to ensure that all “members” (as defined in the Exchange Act) have “fair representation . . . in the selection of its directors and administration of its affairs”
[
13
]
by including member organizations that do not have trading permits. The proposed rule change would allow the Exchange to ensure that it remains in compliance with the cited Exchange Act requirement and make the Operating Agreement consistent with the rules of the Exchange. What is more, the change proposed is based on, and would be consistent with, the wording in the operating agreement of the New York Stock Exchange LLC.
The Exchange believes that the proposed rule change would remove impediments to and perfect the mechanism of a free and open market and a national market system. The proposed Non-Substantive Changes would ensure that market participants can more easily navigate, understand and comply with the governing documents of the Exchange. The proposed rule change to Sections 2.03(a)(iv) and (v) would make the Operating Agreement consistent with the rules of the Exchange and therefore would ensure that market participants can more easily navigate, understand and comply with the governing documents of the Exchange.
The Exchange believes that, by ensuring that the rules accurately identify the registered office in Delaware, making cross-references more accurate, making conforming changes to the title and date of the Operating Agreement, and making the Operating Agreement consistent with the rules of the Exchange, the proposed rule change would reduce potential investor or market participant confusion. The proposed changes would make the Operating Agreement consistent with the rules of the Exchange and therefore would not be inconsistent with the public interest and the protection of investors because investors will not be harmed and in fact would benefit from increased transparency and clarity, thereby reducing potential confusion.
B. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on Burden on Competition
The Exchange does not believe that the proposed rule change will impose any burden on competition that is not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Exchange Act. The proposed rule change is not intended to address competitive issues but rather is concerned solely with making non-substantive changes to the Operating Agreement and making the Operating Agreement consistent with the rules of the Exchange.
C. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on Comments on the Proposed Rule Change Received From Members, Participants, or Others
No written comments were solicited or received with respect to the proposed rule change.
III. Date of Effectiveness of the Proposed Rule Change and Timing for Commission Action
The Exchange has filed the proposed rule change pursuant to Section 19(b)(3)(A)(iii) of the Act
[
14
]
and Rule 19b-4(f)(6) thereunder.
[
15
]
Because the proposed rule change does not: (i) significantly affect the protection of investors or the public interest; (ii) impose any significant burden on competition; and (iii) become operative prior to 30 days from the date on which it was filed, or such shorter time as the Commission may designate, if
(
printed page 68563)
consistent with the protection of investors and the public interest, the proposed rule change has become effective pursuant to Section 19(b)(3)(A) of the Act and Rule 19b-4(f)(6)(iii) thereunder.
[
16
]
At any time within 60 days of the filing of such proposed rule change, the Commission summarily may temporarily suspend such rule change if it appears to the Commission that such action is necessary or appropriate in the public interest, for the protection of investors, or otherwise in furtherance of the purposes of the Act. If the Commission takes such action, the Commission shall institute proceedings under Section 19(b)(2)(B)
[
17
]
of the Act to determine whether the proposed rule change should be approved or disapproved.
IV. Solicitation of Comments
Interested persons are invited to submit written data, views and arguments concerning the foregoing, including whether the proposed rule change is consistent with the Act. Comments may be submitted by any of the following methods:
Electronic Comments
Use the Commission's internet comment form (
https://www.sec.gov/​rules/​sro.shtml
); or
Send an email to
rule-comments@sec.gov
.
Please include file number SR-NYSEAMER-2026-92  on the subject line.
Paper Comments
Send paper comments in triplicate to Secretary, Securities and Exchange Commission, 100 F Street NE, Washington, DC 20549-1090.
All submissions should refer to file number SR-NYSEAMER-2026-92. This file number should be included on the subject line if email is used. To help the Commission process and review your comments more efficiently, please use only one method. The Commission will post all comments on the Commission's internet website (
https://www.sec.gov/​rules/​sro.shtml
). Copies of the filing will be available for inspection and copying at the principal office of the Exchange. Do not include personal identifiable information in submissions; you should submit only information that you wish to make available publicly. We may redact in part or withhold entirely from publication submitted material that is obscene or subject to copyright protection. All submissions should refer to file number SR-NYSEAMER-2026-92 and should be submitted on or before November 20, 2026.
For the Commission, by the Division of Trading and Markets, pursuant to delegated authority.
[
18
]
Sherry R. Haywood,
Assistant Secretary.

Securities and Exchange Commission
[Release No. 34-106741; File No. SR-IEX-2026-41]
October 27, 2026.
Pursuant to Section 19(b)(1)
[
1
]
of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (the “Act”)
[
2
]
and Rule 19b-4 thereunder,
[
3
]
notice is hereby given that, on October 14, 2026, the Investors Exchange LLC (“IEX” or the “Exchange”) filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission (the “Commission”) the proposed rule change as described in Items I and II below, which Items have been prepared by the self-regulatory organization. The Commission is publishing this notice to solicit comments on the proposed rule change from interested persons.
I. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Terms of Substance of the Proposed Rule Change
Pursuant to the provisions of Section 19(b)(1) under the Act,
[
4
]
and Rule 19b-4 thereunder,
[
5
]
the Exchange is filing with the Commission a proposed rule change to amend the Exchange's fee schedule applicable to Options Members
[
6
]
(“Options Fee Schedule”) pursuant to IEX Rules 15.110(a) and (c) to adopt transaction fees and routing fees, and to update the Preface and Definitions sections of the Options Fee Schedule. Changes to the Options Fee Schedule pursuant to this proposal are effective upon filing.
[
7
]
The text of the proposed rule change is available at the Exchange's website at
https://www.iexexchange.io/​resources/​regulation/​rule-filings
and at the principal office of the Exchange.
II. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Purpose of, and the Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
In its filing with the Commission, the self-regulatory organization included statements concerning the purpose of and basis for the proposed rule change and discussed any comments it received on the proposed rule change. The text of these statements may be examined at the places specified in Item IV below. The self-regulatory organization has prepared summaries, set forth in Sections A, B, and C below, of the most significant aspects of such statements.
A. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Purpose of, and the Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
1. Purpose
In preparation for the October 2, 2026 commencement of trading options on IEX Options, IEX filed a proposed rule change to establish the transaction and routing fees it would charge Options
(
printed page 68574)
Members.
[
8
]
On October 14, 2026, IEX concurrently withdrew the Initial Transaction Fee Filing and replaced it with this proposed rule change, which makes no changes to the fees and credits proposed in the Initial Transaction Fee Filing, but provides additional support and context for certain of the fees and credits. Thus, this filing also (i) defines terms in the Preface and Definitions Sections of the Options Fee Schedule that are used throughout the Options Fee Schedule; (ii) establishes transaction fees and credits applicable to all Options Members trading on IEX Options (“Transaction Fees and Credits”); and (iii) establishes routing fees applicable to all Options Members trading on IEX Options who route orders to away exchanges (“Linkage Routing Fees”).
Updates to Preface Section
The Options Fee Schedule has a Preface section that currently has one paragraph, which provides information about billing disputes. The Exchange proposes to add a new paragraph directly following the billing disputes paragraph, which describes the rounding of fees that the Exchange would calculate on the basis of transaction volume. Specifically, the Exchange proposes to add a paragraph with the heading “Rounding,” which explains that the Exchange would apply the applicable fee rate to the sum of an Option Member's volume for the month and where a fractional cent occurs, the Exchange would round up to the nearest whole cent for purposes of computing the Option Member's invoice. The proposed text reads in full:
All volume for the month will be summed and the applicable rate applied. In those cases where a fractional cent occurs, the Exchange will round up to the nearest whole cent for purposes of computing the invoice.
The Exchange believes that including this Rounding paragraph in the Preface to the Options Fee Schedule provides clarity about how the Exchange computes fees. The Exchange's proposed language is consistent with similar language included in the fee schedule of one other exchange.
[
9
]
Updates to Definitions Section
The Exchange includes a Definitions section at the beginning of the Options Fee Schedule for terms that are used throughout the Options Fee Schedule. The purpose of the Definitions section is to streamline the Options Fee Schedule by placing many of the defined terms used in the Options Fee Schedule in one location. For ease of reference and readability, the Exchange proposes adding several definitions to the Definitions section of the Options Fee Schedule, all of which relate to the Transaction Fees and Credits section of the Options Fee Schedule. Many of the defined terms are also defined in the IEX Options Rules, particularly in Rule 17.100. IEX proposes arranging the following definitions in alphabetical order with the previously defined terms in the Options Fee Schedule:
[
10
]
An “Away Market Maker” for the purposes of this fee schedule shall mean a non-IEX Market Maker.
A “Broker-Dealer” means an individual or organization registered with the Commission in accordance with Section 15(b)(1) of the Exchange Act or a foreign broker or dealer exempt from such registration pursuant to Rule 15a-6 under the Exchange Act. See Rule 28.100.
The “Exchange System” or “System” means the automated trading system used by IEX Options for the trading of options contracts. See Rule 22.100(a).
A “Firm” means a Broker-Dealer that is not registered as a Market Maker that is an Options Member of the Exchange. See Rule 28.100.
A “Non-Penny” option refers to option classes that do not participate in the Penny Interval Program, as described in Rule 22.140.
A “Non-Priority Customer” means anyone who is not a “Priority Customer.”
A “Penny” option refers to option classes that participate in the Penny Interval Program, as described in Rule 22.140.
A “Priority Customer” means any person or entity that is not: (A) a broker or dealer in securities; or (B) a Professional.
A “Professional” means any person or entity that (A) is not a broker or dealer in securities; and (B) places more than 390 orders in listed options per day on average during a calendar month for its own beneficial account(s).
The “Step Up Mechanism” is a feature within the System that provides automated order handling in designated classes trading for qualifying orders that are not automatically executed by the System. See Rule 22.270.
IEX notes that other exchanges similarly set forth certain definitions of terms used in their fee schedules in definitions sections in their respective fee schedules.
[
11
]
Transaction Fees and Credits
IEX Options generally operates a “Maker-Taker” model, whereby it provides credits to Options Members that provide liquidity and charges fees to those that remove liquidity. The proposed credits and fees vary depending on the capacity of the two sides to a transaction, whether the applicable options class participates in the Penny Interval Program (“Penny Classes”)
[
12
]
or does not participate in the Penny Interval Program (“Non-Penny Classes”),
[
13
]
and whether the transaction adds or removes liquidity from the IEX Options Book.
Section I of the Options Fee Schedule, which is titled “Transaction Fees and Credits,” is currently “Reserved.” IEX proposes to delete the word “Reserved” and replace it with language describing the transaction fees and credits in this fee proposal. Specifically, IEX proposes to begin Section I with the words “The following transaction rates apply to all options classes. Listed rates are per contract.
Credits are indicated by parentheses ( ).” This introductory text will be followed by Section I.A (“Options Transaction Fees and Credits”) that has two tables showing fees and credits for Penny Classes and for Non-Penny Classes followed by some additional text, which is followed by Section I.B (“Linkage Routing Fees”) that has a table showing fees for routing Penny Class and Non-Penny Class options.
(
printed page 68575)
IEX's proposed transaction fees and credits for Penny Classes do not differentiate between the capacity of the counterparties to the transaction. The following fees shall apply to executions of Penny Classes:
A Priority Customer that adds liquidity will receive a $0.32 credit per contract, and a Priority Customer that removes liquidity will pay a $0.34 fee per contract.
A Professional that adds liquidity will receive a $0.28 credit per contract, and a Professional that removes liquidity will pay a $0.40 fee per contract.
A Market Maker that adds liquidity will receive a $0.26 credit per contract, and a Market Maker that removes liquidity will pay a $0.43 fee per contract.
An Away Market Maker that adds liquidity will receive a $0.22 credit per contract, and an Away Market Maker that removes liquidity will pay a $0.45 fee per contract.
A Firm/Broker-Dealer that adds liquidity will receive a $0.26 credit per contract, and a Firm/Broker-Dealer that removes liquidity will pay a $0.40 fee per contract.
IEX's proposed transaction fees and credits for Non-Penny Classes differentiate between the capacity of the counterparties to the transaction, as described below. Specifically, IEX proposes to charge different transaction fees and credits to the Options Member depending on whether its counterparty in a transaction is a Priority Customer or a Non-Priority Customer. The following fees and credits shall apply to executions of Non-Penny Classes:
A Priority Customer that adds liquidity will receive a $0.70 credit per contract if the counterparty is a Non-Priority Customer and pay $0.00 per contract if the counterparty is a Priority Customer; a Priority Customer that removes liquidity will receive an $0.85 credit per contract if the counterparty is a Non-Priority Customer and pay $0.00 per contract if the counterparty is a Priority Customer.
A Professional that adds liquidity will pay $0.00 per contract if the counterparty is a Non-Priority Customer and pay $0.95 per contract if the counterparty is a Priority Customer; a Professional that removes liquidity will pay $0.25 per contract if the counterparty is a Non-Priority Customer and pay $0.95 per contract if the counterparty is a Priority Customer.
A Market Maker that adds liquidity will receive a $0.10 credit per contract if the counterparty is a Non-Priority Customer and pay $0.95 per contract if the counterparty is a Priority Customer; a Market Maker that removes liquidity will pay $0.25 per contract if the counterparty is a Non-Priority Customer and pay $0.95 per contract if the counterparty is a Priority Customer.
An Away Market Maker that adds liquidity will pay $0.00 per contract if the counterparty is a Non-Priority Customer and pay $0.95 per contract if the counterparty is a Priority Customer; an Away Market Maker that removes liquidity will pay $0.25 per contract if the counterparty is a Non-Priority Customer and pay $0.95 per contract if the counterparty is a Priority Customer.
A Firm/Broker-Dealer that adds liquidity will pay $0.00 per contract if the counterparty is a Non-Priority Customer and pay $0.95 per contract if the counterparty is a Priority Customer; a Firm/Broker-Dealer that removes liquidity will pay $0.25 per contract if the counterparty is a Non-Priority Customer and pay $0.95 per contract if the counterparty is a Priority Customer.
IEX proposes to add language immediately after the Options Transaction Fees and Credits section explaining that orders that are exposed and execute via the Step Up Mechanism will be assigned the applicable fee or credit associated with removing liquidity, while orders that execute against an order exposed via the Step Up Mechanism will be assigned the applicable fee or credit associated with adding liquidity.
IEX also proposes adding a second paragraph that explains that transaction fees and credits associated with executions that occur as part of the Opening Process described in Rule 22.160 are waived.
Linkage Routing Fees
The Exchange proposes to assess Linkage Routing Fees on orders routed to other options exchanges. The amount of the applicable fee will be based on whether the order is in a Penny Class or Non-Penny Class. The Exchange proposes to charge a fee of $1.20 for Penny Class options routed to another options exchange and $1.63 for Non-Penny Class options routed to another options exchange.
The purpose of the proposed Linkage Routing Fees is to offset costs incurred by IEX Options when routing orders to other options exchanges on behalf of Options Members. In determining its proposed Linkage Routing Fees, the Exchange took into account transaction fees and credits assessed by the away markets to which the Exchange routes orders, as well as the Exchange's clearing, administrative, regulatory, and technical costs associated with routing orders to an away market. The Exchange will use unaffiliated routing brokers to route orders to the away markets; the costs associated with the use of these services are reflected in the Linkage Routing Fees specified in the Fee Schedule.
2. Statutory Basis
IEX believes that the proposed rule change is consistent with the provisions of Section 6(b) of the Act
[
14
]
in general and furthers the objectives of Section 6(b)(4) of the Act,
[
15
]
in particular, in that it is designed to provide for the equitable allocation of reasonable dues, fees, and other charges among its members and other persons using its facilities. In addition, the Exchange believes that the proposed fees are consistent with the purposes of Section 6(b)(5)
[
16
]
of the Act in that they are designed to promote just and equitable principles of trade, to foster cooperation and coordination with persons engaged in regulating, clearing, settling, processing information with respect to, and facilitating transactions in securities, to remove impediments to a free and open market and national market system, and, in general, to protect investors and the public interest, and particularly, are not designed to permit unfair discrimination between customers, issuers, brokers, or dealers.
IEX Options operates in a highly fragmented and competitive market in which market participants can readily direct order flow to competing venues if they deem fee levels at a particular venue to be excessive or incentives to be insufficient, and the Exchange represents only a small percentage of the overall market. Accordingly, competitive forces constrain the Exchange's transaction fees and credits, and market participants can readily trade on competing venues if they deem pricing levels at those other venues to be more favorable. The Exchange believes the proposal reflects a reasonable and competitive pricing structure which will promote price discovery and enhance liquidity and market quality on the Exchange to the benefit of all Options Members and market participants. Additionally, the Exchange believes these fees are reasonable, equitable and not designed to permit unfair discrimination because these fees will apply equally to similarly situated Options Members for transactions executed in the same capacity, options class, liquidity role and applicable counterparty category.
(
printed page 68576)
As a threshold matter, the Exchange notes that it has structured its options transaction fee structure to incentivize the types of order flow the Exchange believes will enhance liquidity on IEX Options overall, in a manner that is consistent with the maintenance of a fair and orderly market.
The Exchange believes that it is reasonable, equitable and not designed to permit unfair discrimination, to offer its highest credits and lowest fees for Penny Class transactions to Priority Customers ($0.32 credit per contract to a Priority Customer that adds liquidity; $0.34 fee per contract to a Priority Customer that removes liquidity) because the Exchange believes that Priority Customer order flow enhances liquidity on the Exchange for the benefit of all market participants.
[
17
]
Moreover, the options industry has a long history of providing preferential pricing to Priority Customers.
[
18
]
Additionally, the Exchange notes that these fees are comparable to the fees and credits other options exchanges apply to Priority Customers adding and removing liquidity in Penny Class options.
[
19
]
The Exchange also believes that it is reasonable, equitable and not designed to permit unfair discrimination, in a transaction in a Penny Class option, to offer a $0.28 credit per contract to a Professional that adds liquidity, and to charge a $0.40 fee per contract to a Professional that removes liquidity. Specifically, the Exchange does not believe it is inequitable or unfairly discriminatory to assess lower credits and higher fees to Professionals, compared to Priority Customers, because there is a greater level of proficiency associated with Professionals due to the frequency upon which they access the market. Additionally, IEX notes that other exchanges also have a similar fee structure in Penny Class options where Priority Customers and Professionals (
i.e.,
customers) are subject to preferential rates compared to other types of market participants.
[
20
]
Thus, the Exchange does not believe it is inequitable or unfairly discriminatory to offer a lower fee or higher credit to Priority Customers and Professionals than it offers to other market participants.
The Exchange believes that it is reasonable, equitable and not designed to permit unfair discrimination for the Exchange, in a transaction in a Penny Class option, to offer a $0.26 credit per contract to a Firm/Broker-Dealer that adds liquidity, and to charge a $0.40 fee per contract to a Firm/Broker-Dealer that removes liquidity. IEX notes that it is not uncommon for options exchanges to charge different rates to different non-customers based upon their trading capacity, such as the proposed fees (credits) which are higher (lower) than those charged to customers but lower (higher) than those charged to other non-customer type market participants.
[
21
]
Additionally, IEX notes that these fees are comparable to the fees and credits other options exchanges apply to Firms/Broker-Dealers adding and removing liquidity in Penny Class options.
[
22
]
The Exchange also believes that it is reasonable, equitable and not designed to permit unfair discrimination for the Exchange, in a transaction in a Penny Class option, to offer a $0.26 credit per contract to a Market Maker that adds liquidity, and to charge a $0.43 fee per contract to a Market Maker that removes liquidity. The Exchange believes that the proposed fee structure is consistent with the Act because it is designed to incentivize Market Makers to provide competitively priced liquidity on IEX Options. The Exchange further believes that the differences in fees and credits for Market Makers, as compared to Professionals and Firms/Broker-Dealers, is reasonable, equitable and not designed to permit unfair discrimination because it reflects each type of market participant's level of sophistication and typical liquidity adding or removing role. More specifically, the proposed credit for Market Makers and Firms/Broker-Dealers is designed to incentivize these professional market participants to provide tight and deep quotes in Penny Class options. Similarly, the proposed fees for removing liquidity reflect the trading activity in which the Exchange expects such market participants to generally engage. Specifically, Market Makers are sophisticated market participants, and their role is generally to provide rather than take liquidity, while Professionals and Firms/Broker-Dealers often seek to take liquidity provided by Market Makers. Additionally, the Exchange notes that these proposed rates are comparable to the fees and credits other options exchanges apply to Market Makers adding and removing liquidity in Penny Class options.
[
23
]
The Exchange also believes that it is reasonable, equitable and not designed to permit unfair discrimination, in a transaction in a Penny Class option, to offer its least attractive fees and credits to Away Market Makers. The Exchange understands that Away Market Makers are generally as sophisticated as Market Makers but are not subject to Market Makers' obligations.
[
24
]
Thus the Exchange believes it is consistent with the Act to assess Away Market Makers its lowest credits and highest fees for Penny Class transactions. IEX notes that an Away Market Maker could register with IEX Options as a Market Maker, which would make it eligible for Market Maker fees and credits. Additionally, IEX notes that its Away Market Maker fees are comparable to the fees and credits other options exchanges apply to Away Market Makers for adding and
(
printed page 68577)
removing liquidity in Penny Class options.
[
25
]
The Exchange also believes that it is reasonable, equitable and not designed to permit unfair discrimination for the Exchange, in a transaction in a Non-Penny Class option, to offer a $0.70 credit per contract to a Priority Customer that adds liquidity with a Non-Priority Customer counterparty; charge $0.00 per contract to a Priority Customer that adds liquidity in a transaction with a Priority Customer counterparty; offer an $0.85 credit per contract to a Priority Customer that removes liquidity in a transaction with a Non-Priority Customer counterparty; and charge $0.00 per contract to a Priority Customer that removes liquidity in a transaction with a Priority Customer counterparty, because these fees are comparable to the fees and credits other options exchanges apply to Priority Customers adding and removing liquidity in Non-Penny Class options.
[
26
]
Additionally, the Exchange believes that providing relatively higher credits for Priority Customer trades
[
27
]
with Non-Priority Customer counterparties in Non-Penny Class options and charging relatively higher fees to the Non-Priority Customer counterparties
[
28
]
is consistent with the purposes of the Act because, as described above, the Exchange believes that Priority Customer liquidity benefits all market participants by providing more trading opportunities, which can attract Market Makers and other market participants.
[
29
]
IEX also believes that an increase in the activity of Priority Customers would in turn facilitate tighter spreads, which may cause an additional corresponding increase in order flow from Market Makers and other market participants. Moreover, as discussed above, the options industry has a long history of providing preferential pricing to Priority Customers.
[
30
]
Finally, all fee and credit amounts proposed to apply to Priority Customers will be applied equally to all Priority Customers. Thus, the Exchange believes that it is reasonable, equitable and not designed to permit unfair discrimination for the Exchange to incentivize Priority Customer orders with the higher credits and lower fees contained in this proposal.
The Exchange also believes that it is reasonable, equitable and not designed to permit unfair discrimination for the Exchange, in a transaction in a Non-Penny Class option, to charge $0.00 per contract to a Professional that adds liquidity in a transaction with a Non-Priority Customer counterparty; charge $0.95 per contract to a Professional that adds liquidity in a transaction with a Priority Customer counterparty; charge $0.25 per contract to a Professional that removes liquidity in a transaction with a Non-Priority Customer counterparty; and charge $0.95 per contract to a Professional that removes liquidity in a transaction with a Priority Customer counterparty, because these fees are comparable to the fees and credits other options exchanges apply to Professionals adding and removing liquidity in Non-Penny Class options.
[
31
]
The Exchange also believes that it is reasonable, equitable and not designed to permit unfair discrimination for the Exchange, in a transaction in a Non-Penny Class option, to offer a $0.10 credit per contract to a Market Maker that adds liquidity in a transaction with a Non-Priority Customer counterparty; charge $0.95 per contract to a Market Maker that adds liquidity in a transaction with a Priority Customer counterparty; charge $0.25 per contract to a Market Maker that removes liquidity in a transaction with a Non-Priority Customer counterparty and charge $0.95 per contract to a Market Maker that removes liquidity in a transaction with a Priority Customer counterparty, because these fees are comparable to the fees and credits other options exchanges apply to Market Makers adding and removing liquidity in Non-Penny Class options.
[
32
]
The Exchange also believes that it is reasonable, equitable and not designed to permit unfair discrimination for the Exchange, in a transaction in a Non-Penny Class option, to charge $0.00 per contract to an Away Market Maker that adds liquidity in a transaction with a Non-Priority Customer counterparty; charge $0.95 per contract to an Away Market Maker that adds liquidity in a transaction with a Priority Customer counterparty; charge $0.25 per contract to an Away Market Maker that removes liquidity in a transaction with a Non-Priority Customer counterparty; and charge $0.95 per contract to an Away Market Maker that removes liquidity in a transaction with a Priority Customer counterparty, because these fees are comparable to the fees and credits other options exchanges apply to Away Market Makers adding and removing liquidity in Non-Penny Class options.
[
33
]
The Exchange also believes that it is reasonable, equitable and not designed to permit unfair discrimination for the Exchange, in a transaction in a Non-Penny Class option, to charge $0.00 per contract to a Firm/Broker-Dealer that adds liquidity in a transaction with a Non-Priority Customer counterparty; charge $0.95 per contract to a Firm/Broker-Dealer that adds liquidity in a transaction with a Priority Customer counterparty; charge $0.25 per contract to a Firm/Broker-Dealer that removes liquidity in a transaction with a Non-Priority Customer counterparty; and charge $0.95 per contract to a Firm/Broker-Dealer that removes liquidity in a transaction with a Priority Customer counterparty, because these fees are comparable to the fees and credits other options exchanges apply to Firm/Broker-Dealers adding and removing liquidity in Non-Penny Class options.
[
34
]
(
printed page 68578)
Further, the Exchange believes it is appropriate, reasonable, and consistent with the Act to specify in its Fee Schedule that orders that are exposed and execute via the Step Up Mechanism will be assigned the applicable fee or credit associated with removing liquidity, while orders that execute against an order exposed via the Step Up Mechanism will be assigned the applicable fee or credit associated with adding liquidity, because other options exchanges specify in their fee schedules that they treat executions that occurred within their step up mechanisms in the identical manner.
[
35
]
Furthermore, the Exchange believes it is appropriate, reasonable, and consistent with the Act to waive any transaction fees and credits associated with executions that occur as part of the Opening Process, because other options exchanges also waive transaction fees and credits associated with executions that occur as part of their opening processes.
[
36
]
The Exchange also believes that the Exchange's proposed Linkage Routing Fees for orders routed to other options exchanges ($1.20 for Penny Class option contracts and $1.63 for Non-Penny Class option contracts) are appropriate, reasonable, and consistent with the Act. As discussed in the Purpose section, the proposed Linkage Routing Fees are designed to offset costs incurred by IEX Options when routing orders to other options exchanges on behalf of Options Members. In determining its proposed Linkage Routing Fees, the Exchange took into account transaction fees and credits assessed by the away markets to which the Exchange routes orders, as well as the Exchange's clearing, administrative, regulatory, and technical costs associated with routing orders to an away market, and the costs associated with the use of unaffiliated routing brokers to route orders to the away markets. Further, the Exchange notes that its Linkage Routing Fees are identical to the fees charged by MEMX for routing Penny and Non-Penny Classes to away exchanges.
[
37
]
Finally, the Exchange believes that it is reasonable to update the Preface and Definitions sections of the Options Fee Schedule, because the additional language will clearly set forth the terms used in the Transaction Fees portion of the Options Fee Schedule. Further, the Exchange believes this section is equitable and not unfairly discriminatory because the definitions section (as part of the Options Fee Schedule) will be distributed to all Options Members, so that all Options Members will have equal clarity on fees charged and credits provided.
For the reasons discussed above, the Exchange believes that its proposed changes to the Options Fee Schedule satisfy the requirements of Sections 6(b)(4)
[
38
]
and 6(b)(5)
[
39
]
of the Act in that they provide for the equitable allocation of reasonable dues, fees and other charges among Options Members and other persons using its facilities and are not designed to unfairly discriminate between customers, issuers, brokers, or dealers. As described more fully below in the Exchange's statement regarding the burden on competition, the Exchange believes that its transaction pricing is subject to significant competitive forces, and that the proposed fees and credits described herein are appropriate to address such forces.
B. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on Burden on Competition
IEX does not believe that the proposed rule change will result in any burden on competition that is not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Act.
As a new entrant in the already highly competitive environment for options trading, the Exchange believes that the proposed changes would encourage the submission of additional order flow to a public exchange, thereby promoting market depth, execution incentives and enhanced execution opportunities, as well as price discovery and transparency for all Options Members. IEX Options proposes transaction fees, credits, and routing fees that are comparable to transaction fees, credits and routing fees assessed by other options exchanges. As a result, the Exchange believes that the proposal will have a positive effect on competition.
The Exchange does not believe that the proposed rule change will impose any burden on intramarket competition that is not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Act because the proposed fees and credits will apply equally to similarly situated Options Members for transactions executed in the same capacity, options class, liquidity role and applicable counterparty category. The proposed pricing structure is intended to encourage participants to trade on IEX Options by providing credits that are comparable to those offered by other exchanges as well as providing competitive fees. The Exchange believes that the proposed credits and fees will help to encourage Options Members to send orders to the Exchange to the benefit of all Exchange participants. As the proposed fees and credits are equally applicable to all similarly situated market participants, the Exchange does not believe there is any burden on intramarket competition. Further, as discussed in the Statutory Basis section, while different fees are assessed to different market participants based upon the market participant's capacity (or in the case of Non-Penny Classes, based upon the capacities of both parties to the transaction), these different market participants have different obligations to the Exchange. Additionally, as discussed in the Statutory Basis, the fees are designed to incentivize market participants to engage in the trading activity that is most common for each type of market participant.
The Exchange does not believe that the proposed rule change will impose any burden on intermarket competition that is not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Act. To the contrary, the Exchange believes that the proposed pricing structure will increase competition and is intended to draw volume to the Exchange as it commences operations. The Exchange believes that the ever-shifting market share among the exchanges from month to month demonstrates that market participants can shift order flow or discontinue or reduce use of certain categories of products, in response to new or different pricing structures being introduced into the market. Accordingly, competitive forces constrain the Exchange's transaction fees and credits, and market participants can readily trade on competing venues if they deem pricing levels at those other venues to be more favorable. Currently, no single registered options exchange has more than approximately 19% of the total market share of
(
printed page 68579)
executed volume of listed options trading.
[
40
]
As a new exchange, the Exchange expects to face intense competition from existing exchanges. The proposed pricing structure is intended to encourage market participants to trade on the Exchange by providing credits and assessing fees that are comparable to those offered by other exchanges, which the Exchange believes will help to encourage Options Members to send orders to the Exchange to the benefit of all Exchange participants.

A. Overview of Information Collection
Title of Information Collection:

Description of the need for the information and proposed use:
This is a request for a revision of a currently approved collection for HUD to require applicants and tenants to sign the form HUD-9886-A. The information collected through this PRA assist public housing agencies (PHAs) in eligibility determinations for applicable HUD-assisted housing programs and assist HUD in managing and monitoring these programs. Applicants and tenants applying for or receiving assistance in the Housing Choice Voucher, Public Housing, or Section 8 Moderate Rehabilitation programs are required to sign the Authorization for the Release of Information/Privacy Act Notice (Public and Indian Housing form HUD-9886-A).
Further, this PRA covers the burden associated with the verification required by Section 214 of the Housing and Community Development Act of 1980, as amended, (
42 U.S.C. 1436a
), which prohibits HUD from making financial assistance available to persons who are ineligible for assistance with respect to citizenship or non-citizen immigration status and applies to both applicants for assistance and persons already receiving assistance under: (1) Section 235 of the National Housing Act (the Section 235 Program); (2) Section 236 of the National Housing Act (tenants paying below market rent only) (the Section 236 Program); (3) Section 101 of the Housing and Urban Development Act of 1965 (the Rent Supplement Program); and the United States Housing Act of 1937—(i) HUD's Public Housing Programs; (ii) Section 8 Housing Assistance Programs; and (iii) the Housing Development Grant Programs (with respect to low income units only). This PRA covers the following programs under Section 214: Housing Choice Voucher, Public Housing, and Section 8 Moderate Rehabilitation. Though there is no OMB form associated with the requirements of Section 214, the burden associated with the verification is included in this PRA, because for U.S. citizens or U.S. nationals, each family member, regardless of age, must submit a signed declaration of U.S. citizenship or U.S. nationality. For noncitizens who are 62 years of age or older and receiving assistance or applying for assistance, they must provide a signed declaration of eligible immigration status and proof of age document. For all other noncitizens, they are required to submit: (1) a signed declaration of eligible immigration status; (2) the original of a document designated by U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) as acceptable evidence of immigration status; and (3) a signed verification consent form.

Title of Information Collection:

OMB Approval Number:

Type of Request:

Form Number:

Description of the need for the information and proposed use:
EPIC automates the collection of the Capital Fund program Five-Year Plan and Annual Statement/Budget/Performance and Evaluation (P&E) forms from grantees. These required forms were previously collected in hard copy on Forms HUD-50075.1 and HUD-50075.2 under collection OMB control number 2577-0157. These forms collect data on the eventual and actual use of awarded Federal funds. Electronic collection enables the Department to compile and centralize information about the way grantees use Federal funds. Tracking Federal funds paid through the Public Housing Capital Fund, the only Federal funding stream dedicated to the capital needs of the nation's last resort housing option, is crucial to understanding how the Department can properly and efficiently assist grantees to meet the Department's goals in maintaining and improving public housing as a safe, decent, and sustainable housing option for low-income residents. EPIC also automates the collection of signed documents required by
24 CFR part 905
to gain access to funds awarded by HUD. These forms are covered under the Public Housing Capital Fund Program, OMB control number 2577-0157. Finally, EPIC allows PHAs to request additional funding sources, such as Operating Funds for Capital Fund-eligible activities. The EPIC data system is equipped to collect Physical Needs Assessment data, should this data be required in the future. EPIC is equipped to collect information about the Energy Performance Contract process, including energy efficiency improvements. EPIC is equipped to track development of public housing with Federal funds and through other means, including mixed-finance development.

SUMMARY:
The U.S. Department of Commerce (Commerce) determines that Companhia Brasileira de Alumínio and CBA Itapissuma Ltda. (collectively, CBA) made sales of certain aluminum foil (aluminum foil) from Brazil at prices below normal value (NV) during the period of review (POR) November 1, 2023, through October 31, 2024.
DATES:
Applicable October 30, 2026.
FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT:
Robert Hedberg, AD/CVD Operations, Office VI, Enforcement and Compliance, International Trade Administration, U.S. Department of Commerce, 1401 Constitution Avenue NW, Washington, DC 20230; telephone: (202) 482-0955.
SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION:
Background
On May 7, 2026, Commerce published in the
Federal Register
the
Preliminary Results

Analysis of Comments Received
We addressed the issues raised by parties for these final results of review in the Issues and Decision Memorandum. A list of the issues that parties raised, to which we responded in the Issues and Decision Memorandum, is provided in the appendix to this notice.

Preliminary Results.

see
the Issues and Decision Memorandum.

Disclosure
Commerce intends
                    
                     to disclose the calculations and analysis performed in connection with the final results of this administrative review to interested parties within five days of any public announcement or, if there is no public announcement, within five days of the publication date of this notice in the
Federal Register
, in accordance with 19 CFR 351.224(b).
Assessment Rates
Pursuant to section 751(a)(2)(C) of the Act and
19 CFR 351.212(b)(1)
, Commerce shall determine, and U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) shall assess, antidumping duties on all appropriate entries of subject merchandise in accordance with the final results of this review. For CBA, we calculated importer-specific assessment rates on the basis of the ratio of the total amount of dumping calculated for each importer's examined sales and the total entered value of those sales in accordance with
19 CFR 351.212(b)(1)
. Where an importer-specific assessment rate is
de minimis
(
i.e.,
less than 0.5 percent), the entries by that importer will be liquidated without regard to antidumping duties. For entries of subject merchandise during the POR produced by CBA for which it did not know its merchandise was destined for the United States, we will instruct CBP to liquidate unreviewed entries at the all-others rate if there is no rate for the intermediate company(ies) involved in the transaction.
[
6
]
Commerce intends to issue assessment instructions to CBP no earlier than 35 days after the date of publication of the final results of this review in the
Federal Register
. If a timely summons is filed at the U.S. Court of International Trade, the assessment instructions will direct CBP not to liquidate relevant entries until the time for parties to file a request for a statutory injunction has expired (
i.e.,
within 90 days of publication).
Cash Deposit Requirements
The following cash deposit requirements will be effective for all shipments of subject merchandise entered, or withdrawn from warehouse, for consumption on or after the date of publication of this notice in the
Federal Register
, as provided by section 751(a)(2) of the Act: (1) the cash deposit rate for the companies subject to this review will be equal to the company-specific weighted-average dumping margin established in the final results of the review; (2) for merchandise exported by producers or exporters not covered in this review but covered in a prior completed segment of the proceeding, the cash deposit rate will continue to be the company-specific rate published in the completed segment for the most recent period; (3) if the exporter is not a firm covered in this review, a prior review, or the original investigation, but the producer has been covered in a prior completed segment of this proceeding, then the cash deposit rate will be the rate established in the completed segment for the most recent period for the producer of the merchandise; (4) the cash deposit rate for all other producers or exporters will continue to be 13.93 percent, the all-others rate established in the less-than-fair-value investigation of this proceeding.
[
7
]
These cash deposit requirements, when imposed, shall remain in effect until further notice.
Notification to Importers
This notice serves as a final reminder to importers of their responsibility under
19 CFR 351.402(f)(2)
to file a certificate regarding the reimbursement of antidumping duties prior to liquidation of the relevant entries during this POR. Failure to comply with this requirement could result in Commerce's presumption that reimbursement of antidumping duties occurred and the subsequent assessment of double antidumping duties.
Administrative Protective Order (APO)
This notice also serves as a reminder to parties subject to an APO of their responsibility concerning the destruction or return of proprietary information disclosed under APO in accordance with
19 CFR 351.305(a)(3)
, which continues to govern business proprietary information in this segment of the proceeding. Timely written notification of the destruction or return of APO materials or conversion to judicial protective order is hereby requested. Failure to comply with the regulations and terms of an APO is a sanctionable violation.
Notification to Interested Parties
We are issuing and publishing this notice in accordance with sections 751(a)(1) and 777(i)(1) of the Act, and
19 CFR 351.221(b)(5)
.

AGENCY:

ACTION:
Denial of a petition as moot with Recall 26V525.
SUMMARY:
This notice sets forth the reasons for the denial of defect petition (DP26-009) submitted by Mr. Jason Rund (petitioner) to NHTSA's Administrator. The petition requests NHTSA (the Agency) to initiate a defect investigation to determine if an issue with the rear differential (final drive) assembly of 2022 BMW 540i vehicles is causing the rear wheels to decouple from the drivetrain. Following a technical review of the petition and other information, NHTSA's Office of Defects Investigation (ODI) concluded that that the issues raised do not warrant a defect investigation at this time. Accordingly, the Agency has denied the petition.
FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT:
Roy Nelson, Vehicle Defects Division D, Office of Defects Investigation, NHTSA, 1200 New Jersey Avenue SE, Washington, DC 20590. Telephone: 202-940-7086. Email:
roy.nelson@dot.gov
.
SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION:
Introduction
Interested persons may petition NHTSA requesting that the Agency initiate an investigation to determine whether a motor vehicle or an item of replacement equipment does not comply with an applicable motor vehicle safety standard or contains a defect that relates to motor vehicle safety.
49 U.S.C. 30162(a)(2)
;
49 CFR 552.1
. Upon receipt of a properly filed petition, the Agency conducts a technical review of the petition, material submitted with the petition and any additional information.
49 U.S.C. 30162(a)(2)
;
49 CFR 552.6
. The technical review may consist solely of a review of information already in the possession of the Agency or it may include the collection of information from a motor vehicle manufacturer and/or other sources. After conducting the technical review and considering appropriate factors, which may include, but are not limited to, the nature of the complaint, allocation of Agency resources, Agency priorities, the likelihood of uncovering sufficient evidence to establish the existence of a defect, and the likelihood of success in any necessary enforcement litigation, the Agency will grant or deny the petition.
See
49 U.S.C. 30162(a)(2)
;
49 CFR 552.8
.
Background Information
On September 1, 2026, The Office of Defects Investigation (ODI) received a petition dated August 5, 2026, requesting a defect investigation into an alleged defect of the “rear differential” on the Model Year (MY) 2022 BMW 540i. The petition itself can be reviewed at
NHTSA.gov
under ODI number 11761650.
Summary of Petition
The petition cites allegations of loss of motive power and inability to hold the vehicle stationary, originating from a severed drive connection between the driveshaft and the rear wheels.
Office of Defects Investigation Analysis
On August 12, 2026, BMW filed Safety Recall 26V525 which addresses the same condition raised in Petitioner's submission and covers certain 2022-2026 840i, 840i xDrive, 2021-2023 540i, 540i xDrive, M550i xDrive, and 2024-2026 750e xDrive vehicles. The subject of recall 26V525 addresses progressive wear leading to potential failure of the connection between the rear driveshaft and the rear differential. Petitioner's Vehicle Identification Number (VIN) falls within BMW's recall scope and is subject to BMW's reimbursement program.
Consequently, Recall 26V525 renders the petition moot. Therefore, ODI is denying this petition. The agency reserves the right to take additional action if warranted by future circumstances. To review the reports cited in the Closing Resume ODI Report Identification Number document, go to
NHTSA.gov.
